simulations.label: Simulated from a real campus gym (not BU)
simulations.source_period: 2016-12-05, a Monday (-08:00), the gym's default playback day
transformations: Take the gym's readings for 2016-12-05 (source local time, offset kept in the source file).
Every 15 minutes from 6:00 to 24:00 (FitRec's sample hours), take the latest reading at or before that time if it is at most 30 minutes old; otherwise leave the slot empty (never zero).
Place each slot at the same clock time on the demo Monday (a relabelling, not a timezone conversion).
Multiply by 9.0625: the gym's typical high (72 people, its 95% time-weighted percentile) becomes 75% of FitRec's illustrative capacity (870). Round to whole people.
Split each FitRec total across the 21 areas in proportion to their illustrative capacities (largest-remainder rounding), so the areas always add up to the building total.
assumptions: FitRec's time-of-day pattern resembles this gym's on one in-semester Monday.
Area differences are modeled: every area gets the same share of the total all day, so areas don't have independent patterns and never differ in relative busyness except through crowd tolerance.
The scale is a design choice for the demo, not FitRec's real size or capacity.
limits: Not a measurement of FitRec or any area; no queue, equipment or court availability can be read from it.
One source day: it shows a plausible pattern, not BU's typical traffic or a forecast.
The source gym's counting method isn't documented.

simulations.label: Modeled (no dataset)

targets.name: Fenway Dining
targets.hours: no sample hours; simulated 07:00-23:00 like the other halls

transformations: Interpolate linearly between the (hour, share of illustrative capacity) knots: breakfast around 8 AM, lunch around noon, dinner around 6 PM.
Every 15 minutes within each hall's sample hours, multiply by that hall's illustrative capacity and round to whole people.
assumptions: Meal peaks at 8 AM, noon and 6 PM, with dinner the busiest: a modeling choice, not observed behaviour.
All halls share one shape; only their illustrative sizes differ.
limits: No dining dataset was found that could be used; this is a model, not data, and it does not validate real dining patterns.
No seat availability or queue times can be read from it.

simulations.label: Modeled (no dataset)
transformations: Interpolate linearly between the (hour, share of illustrative capacity) knots: a slow morning, a busy afternoon and an evening peak around 7 PM.
Every 15 minutes within the sample hours, multiply by the illustrative capacity and round.
assumptions: A study-day shape typical of a university library: a modeling choice, not observed behaviour.
limits: The library dataset considered (Chapel Hill Public Library) couldn't be used; see its entry.
No seat or quiet-space availability can be read from it.
